mentl/07d4364:
The lambda arc's first ordering put an emit-level "param product" landing
first, on the claim that `(a,b) => e` and `((a,b)) => e` should be one node
because SYNTAX §L1 calls a parameter list a positional product. A fixture
was written for it and seen RED in the syntax battery.

The use sites refute it. Every one of the 57 double-paren lambdas RECEIVES
a tuple, because that is what the idiom is for: flat_map(((h, depth)) =>
…, slots) over a list of pairs, any(((s, _)) => s == slot, …) over a buffer
of pairs. A one-param function of a pair and a two-param function are
different types; the 13-line WAT divergence is two things compiled
correctly; and collapsing them breaks every pair-consuming HOF in the
wheel. The medium's own "function arity mismatch: 1 param(s) vs 2
param(s)" was right, not lagging.

So the fixture is deleted rather than left standing and the peer is
retracted in place — a banked hypothesis is worse than none, and this one
would have licensed a build that broke map over pairs.

What survives is smaller, not larger: all 254 sites the arm-list literal
targets are already one-param (197 `(x) => match x`, 57 `((a,b)) => …`), so
the literal is a one-param dispatch exactly as a match's arms are, and no
arity semantics are touched at all.

Two sizings recorded for the build that follows: only four NodeBody matches
are exhaustive and must gain an arm, and the arm helpers take arms alone so
they reuse as-is; but lowering ends in project_lambda_fn(handle, captures),
which reads the body from the spine columns by handle, so the node must be
a lambda at the column level and its shape is settled by that projector.
A parse-level desugar is not the shortcut it looks like either — it needs
no node, and then mentl fmt renders the literal back as `(x) => match x`
and undoes every converted site.

No .mn changed; the pin does not move.

Both parts of the multi-effect-ev-index-map are complete and proven on three
minimal repros (two single-effect handlers; one handler over two effects
Tier-2; 6-frame deep multi-effect chain) — all green, battery + trace-suite
66/17 unchanged, mentl2 past the fresh_ph out-of-bounds.

Definitive wheel diagnosis (empirical): the wheel CREATES 102 per-effect
evidence entries but FORWARDS 0 — there are 0 ev-slot stores wheel-wide.
derive_ev_slots returns [] for every call because it bails at ty_tag != TFun,
and every callee type on the wheel is NFre (→TVar 104), never TFun (107).
So no evidence threads; every perform reads an unpopulated __state slot;
fresh_ph traps. The micro-repros work because their callee types DO infer
to TFun.

The whole evidence path's first-light blocker therefore reduces to one root:
Hβ.infer.value-type-nfre-on-wheel, with a precise consumer-driven target —
bind the VarRef-at-call-site node to its instantiated TFun scheme so
lookup_ty(callee) == TFun. The dispatch substrate (this handle) is proven
and waiting; resolution feeds it. The effect ROW is the evidence layout, and
it can only lay out what inference has resolved.

Recursive descent parser written in Lux (~280 lines) that produces

sonido/07eca8a:
Hardware benchmarks showed tape at 171% and reverb at 372% of the per-block
CPU budget on STM32H750. Five targeted optimizations:

- allpass: replace libm::sinf (150 cyc) with fast_sin_turns (20 cyc) in
  ModulatedAllpass. Phase tracking converted from radians to turns. Reverb
  uses 8 ModulatedAllpass instances — saves ~33K cycles/block.

- reverb: downgrade FDN delay interpolation from Cubic to Linear. The small
  LFO modulation depth (~1ms) doesn't benefit from 4-point Lagrange — Linear
  is perceptually equivalent but ~4× cheaper per read.

- tape: fix coefficient recomputation bug — lowpass_coefficients() was called
  every sample in apply_level_hf_l/r (cosf+sinf ×2 per channel). Now cached
  with 1 Hz threshold. Saves ~19K cycles/block.

- ringmod: sinf(phase*TAU) → fast_sin_turns(phase). Phase was already in
  turns — the TAU multiply was pure waste.

- vibrato: division by NUM_VIBRATOS → multiplication by precomputed reciprocal
  at 3 call sites.

Also adds fast_cos_turns() to fast_math.rs (cos = sin shifted by 0.25 turns).
Golden regression files regenerated — output changes are from interpolation
mode and sin precision, both inaudible in context.

noodles/07fed11:
The previous commit's comment says the boundary trim keeps one idle voice
per pool. The code kept two while playing. The floor=1 edit was made,
measured, and then silently lost: the A/B script that swapped builds to
compare floors restored its own saved copy at the end, and I took my
backup from the clobbered tree without re-reading the file. So main
shipped a claim its code did not implement.

It mattered more than the number suggests. A settled song carries 1-2
idle voices per pool, so a floor of 2 means the trim disposes NOTHING at
any settled moment — ten consecutive trims left 42/28/14 untouched. It
only ever fired at the boundary itself, where a retired song dumps 4-6
voices into one pool at once, which is exactly why a broken floor still
measured as a win and nothing caught it. At a floor of 1 the same trim
takes 15 idle to 10 and then converges, as an idempotent trim should.

Settled live source counts after sixteen rolls at a 2.5 s cadence, three
runs each: 665-680 with no boundary trim, 559-587 at a floor of 2,
522-545 at a floor of 1. So the floor was worth ~32 sources on top of the
trim's ~100, and the fix is now ~135 fewer running oscillators and
forever-running param ConstantSources than before it.

The guard that missed this is replaced. Bounding idle surplus only bites
when surplus happens to exist at that instant, and it does not: the
broken build passed the check with idleBefore 5 across 12 pools.
trimVoices now RETURNS what it did ({ran, floor, disposed, idleBefore,
idleAfter, pools}), and smoke pins the floor directly — a deterministic
assertion a dead trim cannot pass. Verified by reintroducing the bug:
smoke exits 1 with "the boundary trim did not run at a floor of 1:
{ran:true,floor:2,disposed:0,...}". voiceStats() gained `pools` so the
behavioural half can state its bound.
